sections.label: Hero
sections.notes: accepted by developer: the theme shared container (max-w-[1440px] px-10) is the source of truth, not the Figma 1190px column. Accepted: content left edge 40px vs design 126px (~86px offset, the site-wide convention shared with header/footer per the hero template comment), and the heading therefore setting on one line instead of the design two. Residual differences NOT caused by the container and not addressed: eyebrow sits ~64px lower (hero content is vertically centred; design anchors it higher), background photo offset ~20px (low severity). QA iter-1 recorded pass:false mismatch 0.3179; the no-product-cards discrepancy was expected since section 3 was unbuilt.

sections.label: Product categories
sections.notes: accepted by developer after 3 QA iterations (best 36.35%, recorded 43.93%). Block extended additively: columns gained a 4 option, plus new surface and overlapTop controls - all default to the previous behaviour so the homepage instance is unchanged. Four-up cards also get a near-square image frame and a one-line label, conditional on columns=4. Remaining differences, none fixable in the block: (1) CONTENT - the WooCommerce category thumbnails are lifestyle photographs, the design shows white product cut-outs; replacing them is a client content task and would also change the homepage. (2) Container 1140px vs the design 1190px - the accepted theme convention. (3) Crop boundary - the crop runs 547-996 from the card tops, but the section element starts at 598 where the hero ends, because the cards overhang it; about 51px of the height delta is that boundary, not the build. Verified by pixel sampling that the hero photo is visible between the cards in the design, so the overhang is real.

sections.label: Product spotlight - photo
sections.notes: accepted by developer at 12.12% (best of 9 iterations; 8% threshold). Heights match to 0.16%. The residual is a ~2px vertical offset of the background photograph across the full-bleed band, which is a large enough area to hold the mismatch above threshold on its own, plus ~2px on the copy column. Everything else matches: heading size, weight and three-line wrap, eyebrow, button size and colour, and the scrim reaching solid black where the design does. Two of the nine iterations were regressions of my own making (removing the inner min-height broke the vertical centring; a full-bleed photo scaled it 1.24x past the design, which anchors it at 1159px wide and 105px off the left edge).

sections.label: Hero
sections.notes: accepted by developer at 9.75% (from 10.39%); height exact. cadco-hero extended additively with a body field and a gradient background mode, both defaulting to the previous behaviour - home and products verified unchanged (no body element, scrim present, heights 841 and 523). The body wrapper is rendered only when it has copy or in the editor: an always-rendered one carried mt-6 and would have pushed the button 24px down on both existing heroes. Remaining differences: (1) content left edge 40px vs the frames 193px - the accepted theme container convention, and the dominant share of the mismatch. Note the frames are not consistent with each other here: products insets to 126px, about to 193px. (2) Heading wraps after Trusted rather than after Experience., and is heavier and a step larger; the size, weight and cap all live in the shared heading class, so matching this page would relayout the home and products heroes. (3) The soft blue glow the frame draws under the word Experience. is not rendered - it needs either markup inside the heading or a decorative control, neither of which exists yet. (4) Content sits about 25px lower; the vertical centring is shared.

sections.label: Represented across US and Canada
sections.notes: accepted by developer at 9.80% (from 28.95%); height within 0.8%. Reuses cadco-product-spotlight rather than a new block. That needed three additive controls, all defaulting to the products behaviour and verified against it (both spotlights unchanged at 785 and 620 high with 64 and 40px headings): scale, which switches heading size, padding, column widths and alignment between a product display and a supporting section; imageAspect for the landscape frame; and a conditional CTA, since an unconditional one drew an empty blue button on a section that has none. Remaining differences: content starts at 146px against the frames 193px, the accepted container convention and the dominant share; the image sits 18px right of the frame as a consequence; and the paragraph wraps one word earlier. A 38px heading matches the frame exactly but wraps to three lines in this column and cost more height than the size gained, so 34px stands.
